<module id="edge_detect">
    <description>Detects rising and falling edges in the input signal a and outputs corresponding signals rise and down.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="a">Input signal.</input>
        <output id="rise">Output signal indicating a rising edge.</output>
        <output id="down">Output signal indicating a falling edge.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <!-- Define any necessary parameters here if needed -->
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        // Sequential logic for detecting edges
        reg [1:0] a_reg;
        
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                a_reg <= 2'b00; // Initialize register to 00 on reset
            end else begin
                a_reg <= {a_reg[0], a}; // Shift in new value of 'a'
            end
        end
        
        // Combinational logic for edge detection
        assign rise = (a_reg == 2'b01); // Rising edge detected
        assign down = (a_reg == 2'b10); // Falling edge detected
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Detect rising and falling edges in the input signal 'a' and generate corresponding output signals 'rise' and 'down'.
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock signal 'clk' or negative edge of the reset signal 'rst_n'.
        // Register 'a_reg' stores two bits representing the previous and current values of 'a'.
        // On each positive edge of 'clk', update 'a_reg' with the shifted values of 'a'.
        // Combinational logic to detect rising and falling edges based on the stored values in 'a_reg'.
        // Assign 'rise' to 1 if there's a rising edge detected, otherwise assign it to 0.
        // Assign 'down' to 1 if there's a falling edge detected, otherwise assign it to 0.
    </implementation>
    
    <task>
        // Task definitions can be added here if needed
    </task>
</module>
